condition.narrative: Ensure that not later than six (6) months from the Effective Date, MoT and MRH jointly select a Project Coordinator to carry outthe coordination and implementation of the Project and a Social Development Specialist to carry out the coordination andsupervision of the gender and social aspects of the Project; and
Ensure that said RAP or any of its provisions are not amended, suspended or abrogated as the case may be, without the prioragreement of the Association.

Finance Agreement :Project Coordinator and Social Dev Spec, Schedule 2, Sec I, A, 1(b) of the FA. | Description :The Recipientshall ensure that not later than six (6) months from the Effective Date that the MRH and MoT jointly select a Project Coordinatorto carry out the coordination and implementation of the project and that the GHA appoint a Social Development Specialist to carryout the coordination and supervision of the gender and social aspects of the project. | Due Date :07-January-2019

Prepare prior to the commencement of any works under the Project, a site-specific Environmental and Social Impact Assessment(“ESIA”) and Environmental and Social Management Plan (“ESMP”), satisfactory to the Association, in accordance with theEnvironmental and Social Assessment (“ESA”);

Prior to the commencement of any works under the Project where a Resettlement Action Plan (“RAP”) is required in accordance withthe Resettlement Policy Framework (“RPF”): (i) prepare and carry out consultations on said RAP;(ii) disclose and implement it ina manner satisfactory to the Association; and (iii) provide full compensation as required under the RAP to any persons entitledto said compensation pursuant to the RAP.

The Recipient shall not later than 9 months from the Effectiveness Date, deposit in the said Escrow Account an additional amountnot to exceed three hundred thousand United States Dollars ($300,000) for the purposes of financing the costs in connection withthe implementation of the RAP.

The Recipient shall, not later than June 30, 2023, recruit a third-party service provider under terms of reference satisfactory tothe Association, to conduct a RAP audit to review its overall compliance with the Association safeguards policy.
The Recipient shall, not later than September 30, 2022, hire an independent financial management consultant, under terms andconditions acceptable to the Association, to validate RAP payments

title.narrative: Use of nationwide vehicle crash data recorded online

comment.narrative: The pilot phase (development) of the vehicle crash data base development is completed. The phase 2 (implementation): Payment for National Information Technology Authority (NITA) to host the iMAAP software has been completed. NITA is yet to complete the hosting and broadcasting of the pilot data online for a nationwide access of the crash data. The pilo data was advised to be used since data collection was not done by government due to budgetary constraints.

A total of 1021.06km out of an actual total of 1029.35km have been completed. The total road length at Atebubu was revised to take out road sections classified under trunk roads, reducing the total road from 1048 to 1029km. The breakdown of rehbailitated roads is below:
186.56km under the Atebubu feeder roads package 3 58.4km under the GHA Lot 1 106km under the GHA Lot 2 235.40km under the Additional Financing Lot 1 208.9 under the Additional Financing Lot 2 225.8km under the Additional Financing Lot 3

title.narrative: Implementation of Road Asset Management System (RAMS) for Trunk roads and Feeder roads

comment.narrative: System has been developed and operationalized. A RAMS unit has been set at the ministry of roads and at its agencies. Road asset data for the entire trunk road network of 10,766km as well as project-level feeder road network of 1035km has been inputed into the Wigrams software of the RAMS. System is yet to be run for reporting purposes.
The activity was cancelled due to suspension of tolling in Ghana since 2021

Diagnostic Study of the GHA is completed which flagged the major issues in terms of Institutional reviews and Policy. The Ghana National Roads Authority Act was passed in 2024 and the diagnostic report is purported to have informed this move.
Update of National Transport Policy completed.
